'''Cesare Burali-Forti''' (13 August 1861 – 21 January 1931) was an Italian [[mathematician]], after whom the [[Burali-Forti paradox]] is named.<ref name=SAU>{{cite web |url= https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Burali-Forti/ |title= Burali-Forti |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |website= University of St Andrews: Maths History |publisher= |access-date= September 22, 2025 |quote=}}</ref> He was a prolific writer, with 200 publications.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cesare Burali-Forti's publications |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Extras/Borali-Forti_publications/ |access-date=2024-02-04 |website=Maths History |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life==
Burali-Forti was born in [[Arezzo]], and he obtained his degree from the [[University of Pisa]] in 1884.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Burali-Forti, Cesare {{!}} Encyclopedia.com |url=https://www.encyclopedia.com/science/dictionaries-thesauruses-pictures-and-press-releases/burali-forti-cesare |access-date=2024-02-04 |website=Encyclopedia.com}}</ref>

== Career ==
{{Expand section|There needs to be more information besides "he was known for the [[Burali-Forti paradox]]".|date=February 2024}}
In 1886, after two years of middle-school service in Sicily, Burali-Forti won a competition to become professor of analytic and projective geometry at the military academy in Turin.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Marchisotto |first=Elena |title=The legacy of Mario Pieri in geometry and arithmetic |last2=Smith |first2=James T. |date=2007 |publisher=Birkhäuser Springer [distributor] |isbn=978-0-8176-4603-5 |location=Boston, Mass. New York |page=69}}</ref> He was an assistant of [[Giuseppe Peano]] in [[Turin]] from 1894 to 1896, during which time he discovered a theorem which [[Bertrand Russell]] later realised contradicted a previously proved result by [[Georg Cantor]]. The contradiction came to be known as the [[Burali-Forti paradox]] of Cantorian [[set theory]].

== Personal life and death ==
He married Gemma Viviani on 29 October 1887 and they had a son named Umberto.<ref name="SAU" />

He died in Turin on 21 January 1931.
